title: Charge Density Wave transient states induced by ultrashort hard X-ray pulses
authors: D. Ghoneim, E. Bellec, L. Ortega, V. L. R. Jacques, A. A Sinchenko, P. Wzietek, U. Boesenberg, K. Kazarian, J. Moeller, J. D. Moore, A. Rodriguez-Fernandez, R. Shayduk, A. Zozulya, A. Madsen, D. Le Bolloc'h
abstract: The interaction of quantum systems with ultrashort laser pulses may lead to transient states far from equilibrium. Among these, Charge Density Wave (CDW) systems offer very rich non-equilibrium physics when submitted to ultrashort optical excitations in the infrared regime. In this Letter, we show that CDW systems pumped by ultrashort x-ray pulses excite the system in very different way. The x-ray pump, 6000 times more energetic than a laser pulse, pumping and probing the whole bulk system simultaneously, drives CDW systems in a novel reversible out of equilibrium state. The successive CDW states observed in the NbSe$_3$ system with respect to the arrival of x-ray pulses follow a non-thermal kinetic path. It is characterized by a change in 2k$_F$ wavevector, correlation lengths and electronic gap, as well as a change of dimensionality, all of this takes place within a very long recovery time ranging from 450$ns$ to 0.01$s$. Several scenarios are proposed, including transient nucleation and recombination of charged topological objects.
summary: This work uses hard X-ray pump-probe techniques to study how Charge Density Wave (CDW) materials respond to extreme, non-equilibrium excitation. The findings reveal a unique, non-thermal dynamic pathway characterized by changes in the CDW order parameters over long timescales. This suggests that X-rays can drive the system into exotic states potentially involving charged topological defects.
main_problem: The study investigates the transient, non-equilibrium states induced in Charge Density Wave (CDW) systems when excited by ultrashort hard X-ray pulses, contrasting this with infrared laser excitation.
main_result: X-ray pumping drives the CDW system into a novel, reversible out-of-equilibrium state characterized by a non-thermal kinetic path, involving changes in the CDW wavevector, correlation lengths, and electronic gap over long recovery times.
method: The research employs X-ray pump-probe experiments using hard X-ray beams (XFEL source) to probe the material dynamics, comparing results obtained from pulse number dependence versus temperature dependence.
model_or_system: The physical system is a CDW material, specifically $	ext{NbSe}_3$. The dynamics are analyzed by tracking changes in the CDW order parameters, suggesting the formation of charged topological objects like solitons.
key_observables: CDW wavevector ($2k_F$), correlation lengths ($\xi$), electronic gap ($\Delta$), and the satellite reflection intensity/width ($	ext{HWHM}$).
important_parameters: X-ray pulse energy (6000 times more energetic than laser pulses), long recovery time ($450	ext{ns}$ to $0.01	ext{s}$), and temperature ($T$ vs. pulse number).
main_assumptions: The non-thermal nature of the excitation is confirmed by observing limited deviation in the main Bragg peak, suggesting the dynamics are not dominated by simple thermal heating.
figures_summary: Figures compare the evolution of CDW order parameters ($	ext{ACDW}$, $\delta q_{	ext{CDW}}$, $	ext{HWHM}$) as a function of XFEL pulse number (green dots) versus temperature (blue/orange dots), highlighting the distinct non-thermal response.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting X-ray vs. laser excitation, presents experimental diagnostics using XFEL/Synchrotron sources, details the observation of non-thermal kinetic paths, and proposes theoretical scenarios involving soliton doping to explain the observed changes in CDW order parameters.
why_interesting: The study probes non-equilibrium many-body dynamics in a strongly correlated electronic state (CDW), which is highly relevant to understanding ultrafast energy dissipation and charge transport in correlated materials.
